title: 第十二章 砺锋
content_zh:
寅时未到，陈默便醒了。

    不是惊醒，也不是自然醒，而是身体在某个预设的时刻，自动挣脱了睡眠的束缚。他没有立刻起身，只是静静躺着，在浓稠的黑暗和同伴们沉滞的呼吸声中，感受着体内与昨日的不同。

    那缕暖流，依旧微弱，但在胸口那片新开辟的、狭窄的路径中，流淌得似乎顺畅了些。他心念微动，尝试引导暖流向右手臂流转。比之前快了一丝，也更“听话”了些。虽然依旧无法离体，也无法带来实质的力量增幅，但那种如臂使指的、微弱却清晰的掌控感，是前所未有的。

    他缓缓坐起，没有点灯，在黑暗中摸索着穿上那身最干净、补丁最少的粗布短褂——这是他能拿出的、最“体面”的行头。用冷水仔细擦了脸和手，将有些蓬乱的头发用手指拢了拢，用一根磨光的木筷固定。

    然后，他拿出那块“丁字七十九”的木牌，用细麻绳穿过，挂在脖子上，贴着胸口。木牌的冰凉触感，让他心头最后一丝残留的睡意也消散无踪。

    他走到自己铺位下，拿出那把用旧布层层包裹的柴刀。解开布，冰冷的刀身在黑暗中泛着幽光。他握住刀柄，缠紧的布条带来熟悉的、扎实的触感。他轻轻挥动了一下，刀刃划破空气，发出极轻微的“嘶”声。很顺手。

    他将柴刀重新用布包好，背在身后，用绳子固定。又检查了一下怀里，黑铁磨石在，那株剩下的铁骨草根也在。

    做完这一切，他推开门，走了出去。

    天色还是浓黑，只有东边天际，有一线极其黯淡的灰白。空气依旧闷热，浓云低垂，仿佛随时会压下来。杂役院里一片寂静，只有远处偶尔传来一两声早起的鸡鸣。

    陈默走到水缸边，舀起一瓢凉水，慢慢喝下。冰凉的液体滑过喉咙，压下心头那丝微不可察的悸动。然后，他走到平日站桩的屋檐下，却没有摆开架势，只是静静地站着，望向东方那线逐渐扩散的灰白。

    他在等。等一个时辰，等天光，也等那个时刻的到来。

    时间在寂静中缓慢流淌。天光渐渐亮起，驱散黑暗，露出杂役院低矮破败的轮廓，和远处群山沉默的剪影。但今日的天空，是铅灰色的，云层厚重，不透一丝阳光。

    陆续有杂役起身，打着哈欠，揉着惺忪睡眼，开始一天的劳作。看到陈默穿戴整齐、背着柴刀静静立在屋檐下，有人投来诧异的目光，有人低声议论两句，但大多只是漠然地看一眼，便各忙各的去了。今日，对他们而言，与往日并无不同。

    王虎也起来了，脸色有些苍白，看见陈默，嘴唇动了动，最终什么也没说，只是低头走向井台。

    李大从屋里冲出来，身上那件不知从哪弄来的、明显不合身的旧褂子皱巴巴的，小臂上果然绑着两块歪歪扭扭的木板，用布条缠着，看起来颇为滑稽。他脸色紧张，额角冒汗，看见陈默，眼睛一亮，快步走过来。

    “陈默！你、你都准备好了？”李大声音有些发颤，“我、我怎么觉得心慌得厉害……”

    陈默看了他一眼，点点头：“平常心。”

    “平常心……”李大喃喃重复，擦了把额头的汗，努力想做出个镇定的表情，却比哭还难看。

    卯时初刻，晨钟敲响，沉闷的钟声在群山间回荡。

    陈默最后看了一眼这个他生活了近三年的、破败沉寂的院子，深吸一口气，转身，向院外走去。脚步不疾不徐，踏在尚且湿润的泥土地上。

    “等等我！”李大连忙跟上，差点被自己匆忙的脚步绊倒。

    两人一前一后，走出杂役院，踏上通往主峰方向的青石山道。山道上已经有些和他们一样，前往较技场的人。有穿着杂役短褂的，也有服饰稍好、但绝非宗门正式弟子的少年，彼此间很少交谈，只是沉默地赶路，气氛压抑。

    越靠近主峰，山道越宽阔平整，两旁的建筑也越发气派。飞檐斗拱，朱漆廊柱，虽非核心区域，也已远非杂役院可比。偶尔有身着青色宗门服饰的外门弟子结伴走过，谈笑风生，气息沉凝，目光扫过陈默这些“丁字”号参赛者时，带着毫不掩饰的审视、好奇，或是不加掩饰的轻蔑。

    陈默目不斜视，只是稳步前行。他能感觉到那些目光，像细小的针，扎在皮肤上。但他心静如水。体内那缕暖流，随着他的步伐，在胸口新辟的路径中缓缓流淌，带来一丝微弱却持续的温热感，仿佛在提醒他，昨夜那一声轻微的“啵”，是真实的。

    走了约莫半个时辰，眼前豁然开朗。一片极为开阔的、以巨大青石板铺就的广场出现在面前。广场尽头，是一座巍峨的高台，高台后方，是更加宏伟的殿宇楼阁，隐在晨雾和铅灰色的天幕下，气象森严。这里，便是青云宗外门“较技场”。

    此刻，广场上已是人声鼎沸。黑压压的人群分成泾渭分明的几片。人数最多、气息也最杂的，是和陈默他们一样，来自各杂役院、附属家族或散修背景的“丁字”组参赛者，怕是有两三百人，聚集在广场左侧，被一些身着灰衣的执事弟子约束着，略显混乱。右侧，则是人数较少、但秩序井然、气息明显凝实许多的“丙字”组——那是入门三年内的外门弟子，约莫百余人，一个个挺胸抬头，顾盼自雄。更远处，靠近高台的地方，还有人数更少、但气势更强的“乙字”、“甲字”组，是入门更久、修为更高的外门弟子，他们的比试将在后面进行。

    高台之上，已经摆放了数张座椅，有数位气息深沉、穿着墨绿或深蓝服饰的中年或老者端坐，应是外门的长老或执事。他们神情平淡，目光偶尔扫过下方广场，带着居高临下的淡漠。

    陈默和李大按照指引，挤进了“丁字”组的人群。周围是各种味道：汗味、尘土味、劣质油脂味，还有掩饰不住的紧张呼吸带来的酸气。耳边充斥着压低嗓音的交谈、粗重的喘息、不安的挪动脚步声。陈默寻了个相对人少的角落站定，微微调整呼吸，让自己平静下来。李大小心翼翼地挨着他，眼睛不安地四处张望，身体微微发抖。

    辰时正，高台上一名紫面长须的老者站起身，走到台前。他并未刻意提高声音，但清晰的话语却瞬间压过了场中所有的嘈杂，传入每个人耳中：

    “肃静。”

    两个字，带着不容置疑的威严。广场上瞬间鸦雀无声。

    “青云宗，丁亥年外门小比，现在开始。”紫面老者目光扫过下方，“规矩，尔等入场时已知晓。老夫不再赘言。唯有一点，需谨记：比试切磋，旨在考校进境，点到为止。若有蓄意伤残同门、动用禁器邪术者，严惩不贷！都听明白了？”

    “明白！”下方参差不齐地应道。

    “好。”紫面老者微微颔首，“‘丁’、‘丙’两组，先行混抽。第一轮，较技台东、西各十座，同时进行。念到编号者，即刻上台，十息不至，视作弃权。开始。”

    他话音刚落，高台侧方，两名执事弟子便抬出一个半人高的木箱。另一名执事上前，朗声开始唱号：

    “甲字三台，丁字二十四，对丙字七！”

    “甲字四台，丁字六十一，对丁字一百三十三！”

    “甲字五台……”

    唱号声清晰洪亮，在广场上空回荡。被念到编号的参赛者，或紧张，或兴奋，或忐忑，在周围人复杂的目光注视下，挤出人群，快步走向指定的石台。

    石台高一丈，方圆五丈，以坚硬的黑纹石砌成，表面有简单的阵纹加固，防止劲气过度外泄。每座石台边，都有一名灰衣执事作为裁判。

    比试很快开始。呼喝声、拳脚碰撞声、金铁交鸣声、法术爆裂的轻响，瞬间打破了广场短暂的寂静，混杂成一片嘈杂的声浪。灵力波动虽然微弱杂乱，但成百上千道交织在一起，也让这片区域的空气隐隐震动。
content_en:
Before the Yin hour arrived, Chen Mo woke up.
It is not a sudden awakening, nor a natural awakening, but the body automatically breaks away from the shackles of sleep at a preset moment.He did not get up immediately, but just lay quietly, feeling the difference in his body from yesterday in the thick darkness and the stagnant breathing of his companions.
The warm current was still weak, but it seemed to flow more smoothly in the newly opened, narrow path in the chest.His mind moved slightly, trying to guide the warm current to flow to his right arm.A little faster than before, and more "obedient".Although it is still unable to leave the body and cannot bring about a substantial increase in strength, the weak but clear sense of control that can be felt like an arm is unprecedented.
He sat up slowly, without lighting a lamp, and groped in the darkness to put on the cleanest and least patched coarse cloth jacket - the most "decent" outfit he could come up with.I wiped my face and hands carefully with cold water, gathered my somewhat disheveled hair with my fingers, and fixed it with a polished wooden chopstick.
Then, he took out the wooden sign with "T-shaped seventy-nine", passed it through with a fine hemp rope, and hung it around his neck, close to his chest.The cold touch of the wooden sign made the last remaining drowsiness in his heart dissipate.
He walked under his bunk and took out the hatchet wrapped in layers of old cloth.Untying the cloth, the cold blade glowed in the darkness.He held the handle of the knife, and the tightly wrapped cloth brought a familiar, solid touch.He waved it lightly, and the blade cut through the air, making a very slight "hiss" sound.Very convenient.
He wrapped the hatchet in cloth again, carried it behind his back, and fixed it with a rope.I checked my arms again and saw that the black iron grindstone was there, as well as the remaining iron-bone grass roots.
After doing all this, he opened the door and walked out.
The sky was still dark, except for a line of extremely dim gray on the eastern horizon.The air is still muggy, and the thick clouds hang low, as if they will press down at any time.There was silence in the yard, except for the occasional early rooster crow in the distance.
Chen Mo walked to the water tank, scooped up a ladle of cold water, and drank it slowly.The cold liquid slid down his throat, suppressing the undetectable throbbing in his heart.Then, he walked to the eaves where he usually stood, but did not put on any posture. He just stood quietly and looked at the gradually spreading gray line in the east.
He is waiting.Wait for an hour, wait for the sky, and wait for that moment to come.
Time flows slowly in silence.The sky gradually brightened, dispersing the darkness, revealing the low and dilapidated outline of the courtyard and the silent silhouette of the mountains in the distance.But today's sky is leaden gray, with thick clouds and no sunlight.
One after another, the handymen got up, yawned, rubbed their sleepy eyes, and began to work for the day.Seeing Chen Mo standing quietly under the eaves, neatly dressed and carrying a hatchet on his back, some people cast surprised glances, some whispered a few words, but most of them just looked at him indifferently and went about their business.Today, for them, is no different than before.
Wang Hu also got up, his face was a little pale, and when he saw Chen Mo, his lips moved, but in the end he didn't say anything, he just lowered his head and walked towards the well platform.
Li Da rushed out of the room. He was wearing a wrinkled old coat that he got from nowhere and obviously didn't fit. As expected, there were two crooked wooden boards tied to his forearms and wrapped with strips of cloth. It looked quite funny.His face was tense and sweat was pouring from his forehead. When he saw Chen Mo, his eyes lit up and he walked over quickly.
"Chen Mo! Are you, are you ready?" Li Da's voice was trembling, "I, why do I feel so flustered..."
Chen Mo glanced at him and nodded: "Be normal."
"A normal heart..." Li Da murmured again, wiping the sweat from his forehead and trying hard to make a calm expression, but it turned out to be uglier than crying.
At the first quarter of Mao hour, the morning bell rang, and the dull bell echoed in the mountains.
Chen Mo took one last look at the dilapidated and silent courtyard where he had lived for nearly three years. He took a deep breath, turned around, and walked out of the courtyard.The steps were neither fast nor slow, stepping on the still moist soil.
"Wait for me!" Li Da hurriedly followed, almost tripping over in his own hasty footsteps.
The two of them walked out of the courtyard one after another and stepped onto the bluestone mountain road leading to the main peak.There were already some people on the mountain road who were heading to the competition ground just like them.There were some young men wearing short coats for servants, and some young men with slightly better clothing, but who were by no means formal disciples of the sect. They rarely talked to each other, but just walked on in silence, and the atmosphere was depressing.
The closer you get to the main peak, the wider and smoother the mountain road becomes, and the buildings on both sides become more impressive.The cornices and brackets and the vermilion-lacquered corridors and columns are not the core area, but they are far from comparable to the courtyard.Occasionally, outer sect disciples wearing blue sect attire walked by together, chatting and laughing, with a calm atmosphere. When their eyes glanced at Chen Mo and other "T" contestants, they showed undisguised scrutiny, curiosity, or undisguised contempt.
Chen Mo didn't look sideways and just moved forward steadily.He could feel those gazes, like tiny needles pricking his skin.But his mind was as calm as water.The warm current in his body slowly flowed through the newly opened path in his chest with his steps, bringing a faint but continuous feeling of warmth, as if to remind him that the slight "pop" last night was real.
After walking for about half an hour, my eyes suddenly opened up.An extremely open square paved with huge bluestone slabs appeared in front of them.At the end of the square is a majestic high platform, and behind the high platform are even more magnificent palaces and pavilions, hidden under the morning mist and leaden gray sky, with a formidable atmosphere.This is the "competition ground" of the Qingyun Sect's outer sect.
At this moment, the square was full of people.The dark crowd was divided into distinct groups.The ones with the largest number of people and the most mixed atmosphere were, like Chen Mo and others, the contestants from the "D" group who came from various courtyards, affiliated families or casual cultivators. There were probably two to three hundred people gathered on the left side of the square, being restrained by some deacon disciples in gray clothes, making it slightly chaotic.On the right side, there is the "C" group, which is smaller in number, but more orderly, and has a much more solid aura - they are the outer disciples who have been in the school for three years, about a hundred people, each with their chests raised and their heads raised, looking at themselves.Further away, close to the high platform, there are the "B" and "A" groups with smaller numbers but stronger momentum. They are the outer disciples who have been in school for a longer time and have higher cultivation. Their competition will be held later.
On the high platform, several seats have been placed. There are several middle-aged or old men with deep breaths and wearing dark green or dark blue clothes sitting upright. They should be elders or deacons of the outer sect.Their expressions were dull, and their eyes occasionally glanced at the square below with a condescending indifference.
Chen Mo and Li Da followed the instructions and squeezed into the "T" group.There are various smells around: the smell of sweat, dust, low-quality grease, and the sour smell caused by nervous breathing that cannot be concealed.My ears were filled with the sounds of hushed conversations, heavy breathing, and restless footsteps.Chen Mo found a corner where there were relatively few people and stood there, adjusting his breathing slightly to calm himself down.Li Da stood next to him cautiously, his eyes looking around uneasily, and his body trembling slightly.
At the right time, an old man with purple face and long beard on the high platform stood up and walked to the front of the stage.He did not raise his voice deliberately, but his clear words instantly overwhelmed all the noise in the venue and reached everyone's ears:
"quiet."
Two words, carrying unquestionable majesty.The square fell silent for a moment.
"Qingyun Sect, Dinghai year outer sect competition begins now." The purple-faced old man glanced downwards, "You already knew the rules when you entered the venue. I won't go into details. There is only one thing you need to remember: the competition is aimed at entering the school, and it will end there. Anyone who intentionally maims a fellow sect or uses forbidden weapons and magic will be severely punished! Do you understand?"
"Understood!" The people below responded unevenly.
"Okay." The purple-faced old man nodded slightly, "Two groups of 'D' and 'C' will draw first. In the first round, there will be ten contests in the east and west of Taipei, and they will be held at the same time. Those who read the number will immediately come on stage. If they do not come for ten breaths, they will be deemed to have abstained. Start."
As soon as he finished speaking, two deacon disciples carried out a wooden box half a person's height from the side of the high platform.Another deacon stepped forward and began to sing:
"A means three, D means twenty-four, and C means seven!"
"The number A is four, the number D is sixty-one, and the number D is one hundred and thirty-three!"
"A-character Wutai..."
The sound of the trumpets was clear and loud, echoing over the square.The contestants who had their numbers read out were either nervous, excited, or apprehensive. Under the complicated gazes of the people around them, they squeezed out of the crowd and walked quickly to the designated stone platform.
The stone platform is one foot high and five feet wide. It is made of hard black-grained stone and has simple pattern reinforcement on the surface to prevent excessive leakage of energy.Beside each stone platform, there is a deacon in gray as the referee.
The competition begins soon.The sound of shouts, the clash of fists and feet, the sound of gold and iron, and the soft sound of magic bursting instantly broke the brief silence of the square and mixed into a noisy sound.Although the spiritual power fluctuations were weak and chaotic, hundreds of them were intertwined together, causing the air in this area to faintly vibrate.
